mcq_fix.s: Assertion (A): Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India upheld economic criteria alone as a valid basis for classification. Reason (R): The case upheld the validity of the 103rd Constitutional Amendment Act providing a 10% EWS quota.
mcq_fix.why: case name is Janhit Abhiyan, not 'Janki Janhit Abhiyan'

mcq_drop.why: dubious statement 2: 2006 Act was for central institutions; Thakur left private unaided open
off-topic and oddly worded (Arts 19-27 matched to 'social concerns')

notes_fix.why: case is Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India (2022)

pyq_bad.why: suspect key: Rule of Law is British-derived; US-similar feature is Fundamental Rights

patterns: APPSC asks single-fact article mapping: Right to Equality = Art. 14 (2025), Art. 15 available to citizens only, untouchability = Art. 17.
Exclusion traps: groups not covered by Art. 15 special provisions (aged persons, APPSC 2023).
Amendment-number questions: EWS = 103rd Amendment / 124th Bill; reservation amendments 77th, 81st, 93rd (APPSC 2022).
Group-1 uses long statement items mixing Dicey's rule of law, Art. 361 and Balaji Raghavan.
App MCQs lean heavily on case-law chronology, bench splits and 2026 current affairs that APPSC PYQs rarely touch.
